event_name: Van Leeuwen Ice Cream Dunwoody Opening: $1 Scoops
venue: Van Leeuwen Ice Cream, Park Place Dunwoody
blurb:
⭐ **Featured Event: Van Leeuwen Ice Cream Dunwoody Opening**
📅 Wednesday, August 19 | 11:00 AM – 1:00 PM | Park Place, Dunwoody
🎟️ $1 scoops | [Learn More]()

Van Leeuwen is opening a location right at Park Place in Dunwoody, and they're doing $1 scoops from 11am to 1pm on Wednesday the 19th to celebrate. If you've had Van Leeuwen before, you know the ice cream is legitimately good, not mall-food-court good, actually good.

The timing is a weekday lunch window, so it's not going to work for everyone. But if you work from home or you've got kids home before the school year fully kicks in, it's an easy and cheap reason to get out of the house for an hour. A new neighborhood spot worth knowing about either way.

Get there before the line builds.
scoring_notes: Grand opening with $1 scoops is a genuine one-time event and hyperlocal to Dunwoody. Weekday midday timing limits audience reach significantly. More family-friendly than adult-skewing, but the brand cachet and neighborhood relevance keep it on the list. Works best as a secondary pick, not a lead feature.

blurb:
⭐ **Featured Event: (MC)2 Multicultural Dance Festival**
📅 August 24–29 | 7:00 PM | Atlanta area
🎟️ Ticketed | [Learn More]()

The (MC)2 Multicultural Dance Festival runs August 24 through 29 and brings together Atlanta-based dance companies from different cultural backgrounds onto the same stage. It's curated by George Staib and staibdance, and if you've caught any of their work before, you already know this isn't a school recital situation.

A week-long festival format means you've got multiple nights to work with, which is rare. Pick the night that fits your schedule rather than scrambling to rearrange your calendar around a single show. The programming spans different cultural traditions, so each night can feel pretty distinct from the last.

If you're the kind of person who talks about wanting to see more live arts in Atlanta, here's a specific and easy opportunity to actually do it.
scoring_notes: Educated, culturally engaged Perimeter audience is a natural fit for a curated dance festival. Week-long run adds flexibility and reduces urgency slightly, but the uniqueness of the multicultural format and the Staib curation give it real distinction. Venue details are thin, which limits the blurb somewhat.

event_name: All Shook Up: The Elvis Presley Musical
venue: Marietta's Theatre in the Square, Marietta
blurb:
⭐ **Featured Event: All Shook Up: The Elvis Presley Musical**
📅 Saturday, August 15 | 8:00 PM | Marietta's Theatre in the Square, Marietta
🎟️ Ticketed | [Learn More]()

Elvis songs. A Shakespeare plot. A leather-jacketed stranger rolling into a repressed 1955 Midwestern town and turning everything upside down. That's the setup for All Shook Up, and honestly it works way better than it has any right to.

Theatre in the Square is running this through August 22, so you've got a couple of weekends to make it happen, but Saturday night at 8 is the move if you want the full experience. It's a jukebox musical built on some of the most recognizable songs ever recorded, which means even people who don't usually love theater tend to leave having a good time.

Good date night. Good group outing. If you've been meaning to catch more live theater and keep letting weekends slip by, this one's an easy yes.
scoring_notes: Live theater fits the educated, adult-leaning Perimeter audience well. Elvis catalog gives it broad appeal across age ranges. Multiple weekend run limits the urgency somewhat, but Saturday night at 8pm is a natural featured slot. Good adult skew.

blurb:
⭐ **Featured Event: Cocktail Class at ASW Distillery**
📅 Sunday, August 23 | 2:00 PM – 3:30 PM | ASW Distillery, Atlanta
🎟️ Ticketed | [Get Tickets]()

ASW Distillery runs a cocktail class monthly where you actually get your own bar station, your own tools, and you build three cocktails from scratch with one of their lead mixologists walking you through it. Whiskey, vodka, gin, all featuring ASW's own award-winning spirits.

A Sunday afternoon from 2 to 3:30 is about the right length for this. Long enough to actually learn something, short enough that you still have a Sunday evening. The charcuterie board add-on at checkout is worth mentioning because it's the obvious move if you're going with a partner.

ASW is a legitimate Atlanta craft distillery with a real following. If you've been buying their bottles at Total Wine and wondering what goes into making them, this is the most fun version of that answer.
scoring_notes: Monthly class format slightly reduces uniqueness, but the hands-on experience and adult-only nature are a strong fit for the Perimeter's income level and lifestyle. Sunday afternoon timing is accessible. Good date activity or small group option. Note: this is a recurring monthly class, so featured event is a soft recommendation.

event_name: Atlanta Braves vs Los Angeles Dodgers
blurb:
⭐ **Featured Event: Atlanta Braves vs Los Angeles Dodgers**
📅 Tuesday, August 25 | 7:15 PM | Truist Park, Atlanta
🎟️ Ticketed | [Get Tickets]()

The Dodgers are coming to Truist Park. If you follow baseball even loosely, you know that Los Angeles is one of the most stacked rosters in the league right now, which makes this about as good a midweek matchup as you're going to get all season.

Truist Park is essentially in the Perimeter's backyard, and a Tuesday night game in late August is genuinely one of the better ways to spend a weeknight, especially when the visiting team is actually worth watching. First pitch at 7:15 means you're home by 10 if things move along.

Bring the family, bring a client, or just go with whoever is always down for a ballgame. The Battery has plenty of options for dinner before the first pitch if you want to make a full night of it.
scoring_notes: Braves vs Dodgers is a premium matchup with real draw. Truist Park is walking distance from the Perimeter audience's typical radius. Broad family and adult appeal. Weeknight limits it slightly for families but the $105K income level means taking the family to a game is a casual decision, not a budget one.

venue: Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, Atlanta
blurb:
⭐ **Featured Event: ArtsBridge Foundation Overture Gala**
📅 Thursday, August 27 | 6:00 PM | Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, Atlanta
🎟️ Ticketed | [Get Tickets]()

This year's ArtsBridge Overture Gala is going with an Island Time theme, which means cocktails, live music from A1A (Jimmy Buffett's official tribute band), a live auction, and dancing at one of the nicer rooms in the Atlanta area, Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre.

ArtsBridge does real work, connecting arts education programs to Georgia public school classrooms, so the night has some actual meaning behind the fun. That said, nobody's going to make you feel bad about being there primarily for the Buffett tribute band and an open bar situation.

Thursday night out in late August, good cause, live music, and a room full of people who actually dress up for things. Worth circling on the calendar now before the week fills up.
scoring_notes: Annual gala format with a clear theme and live entertainment hits well for the $105K median income audience. Cobb Energy is a local landmark. Good empty nester and young professional crossover. Charitable angle adds appeal for educated, civic-minded audience. Thursday limits it slightly.

event_name: Movies at The Strand: Mamma Mia and Margaritas!
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb:
⭐ **Featured Event: Movies at The Strand: Mamma Mia and Margaritas!**
📅 Saturday, August 22 | Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
🎟️ Ticketed | [Get Tickets]()

If you've ever watched Mamma Mia at home and wished you were doing it with 400 strangers, a margarita in your hand, and a Mighty Allen Theatre Organ warming things up before the movie starts, well, Saturday is your night.

The Strand is doing a full margarita bar for this one, and they're encouraging you to show up in your flashiest boa if the mood strikes. It's ridiculous in the best way. Meryl Streep, ABBA, Pierce Brosnan attempting to sing, and a room full of people who are absolutely there for it.

The organ pre-show kicks off 30 minutes before showtime, which means you actually want to get there early for once. This is a STEAL for a Saturday night out that doesn't require a reservation six weeks in advance. Grab a group, grab a boa, and go.
scoring_notes: The margarita bar and singalong format make this a genuinely unique, one-night event rather than a standard screening. Strong appeal for the mixed adult crowd, young professionals and empty nesters alike. The Strand is a beloved local venue. High fun factor, low barrier to entry.

event_name: Taste of Jamaica: Interactive Chef's Table
blurb:
⭐ **Featured Event: Taste of Jamaica: Interactive Chef's Table**
📅 Sunday, August 23 | 6:30 PM | Vino Venue, Dunwoody
🎟️ Ticketed | [Get Tickets]()

This isn't a cooking demo where you watch someone else do all the work. The Taste of Jamaica Chef's Table at Vino Venue puts you in the kitchen, hands on, learning the food and the stories and the traditions behind one of the most distinct culinary cultures in the world. Jerk, allspice, scotch bonnet, the whole deal.

For a Sunday night, it's a genuinely fun way to spend a few hours. The format runs 6:30 to 9:00pm, which means you're home at a reasonable hour and you've actually done something worth talking about at the office Monday morning. Vino Venue is a short drive from most of the Perimeter area, and they do this stuff right.

If your idea of a good weekend isn't watching another movie on the couch, this is worth booking. Spots fill up.
scoring_notes: High-income, educated, adult-skewing Perimeter audience is exactly the crowd for an immersive culinary experience. Dunwoody location is hyper-local. Sunday evening timing is ideal. Not a recurring weekly event. Strong adult fit, no kids needed.

event_name: All Shook Up: The Elvis Presley Musical
blurb:
If you grew up knowing every word to 'Hound Dog' or 'Jailhouse Rock,' Marietta Theatre Company has something for you this weekend.

All Shook Up is a full musical built around the Elvis catalog, loosely adapted from Shakespeare's Twelfth Night. The setup is 1955, a guitar-playing stranger rolls into a quiet little town, and everything changes. It's joyful, it's PG, and it gives you nearly every Elvis classic you'd want to hear live on a real stage. Marietta Theatre Company consistently puts out quality productions, and a show like this plays to exactly the crowd that remembers when these songs were on the radio the first time around.

It opens August 14th. Check the Marietta Theatre Company's site for showtimes and grab your seats before the run fills up.
scoring_notes: With a median age of 42 and a heavy established-family and empty-nester skew, an Elvis-catalog musical at a local theater is a strong cultural fit. This audience grew up with the music and has the disposable income and inclination for a night out at a community theater. It's family-friendly (rated PG) without skewing too young. Loses points on uniqueness since it runs as a production over multiple dates, not a single-night event, but it IS a limited theatrical run which makes it more finite than a weekly series.

event_name: Marg & Taco Fest at The Battery Atlanta
venue: Live! at The Battery Atlanta, Atlanta
blurb:
If your idea of a perfect August Saturday involves a margarita in hand, a lineup of local taco trucks, and a mariachi band doing its thing while the sun goes down, this is your weekend.

Marg & Taco Fest is back at Live! at The Battery on August 22nd, and it's a full four hours of exactly what it sounds like. Your ticket gets you two drink tickets right out of the gate, so you're not nickel-and-diming your way through the afternoon. From there, it's outdoor games, a live DJ, local vendors, and enough tacos to make you genuinely reconsider your dinner plans. The Battery's patio setup is already one of the better spots in Cobb for a summer evening, and this one gives you a real reason to be there.

Grab your crew, get there early, and let the mariachi band set the tone. This is the kind of Saturday afternoon that doesn't need much justification.
scoring_notes: East Cobb's $118K median income and mix of established adults and empty nesters fits a ticketed food-and-drink festival at The Battery extremely well. The Battery is already a familiar and comfortable destination for this audience. The two-drink-ticket inclusion makes it feel like good value at this income level without being the main selling point. Loses a point on uniqueness since Marg & Taco Fest has run before, but it's not a weekly recurring event and August 22nd is a specific, distinct date worth flagging.

blurb:
You've probably been to Truist Park for a game. But you haven't done this.

Moonlight Tours give you an after-dark, behind-the-scenes look at one of baseball's best ballparks, starting at the Blue Moon Brewery where you'll hear the brand's baseball backstory and get an insider look at the brewing process. From there it's a guided tour through the park itself, including the press box and the Braves dugout, with a cold Blue Moon in hand the whole way. This one is 21+ and it's not a game night, so the whole vibe is different. Quieter. More intimate. The kind of access you can't get on a normal Saturday with 40,000 people around.

Spots are limited and this doesn't come around often. If you've ever wanted to stand in the dugout without a ticket in a stadium full of strangers, here's your shot.
scoring_notes: The 21+ requirement and the experiential, adult-oriented format fits East Cobb's established adults and empty nesters well. The income level makes a ticketed brewery-plus-ballpark tour a no-brainer from a price sensitivity standpoint. Scores very high on uniqueness because this is genuinely a behind-the-scenes access event that most Braves fans have never experienced. Audience match score of 7 reflects that it skews adult-only and won't resonate with the family segment of the newsletter's readership.

event_name: Movies at The Strand: Ferris Bueller's Day Off
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb:
Here's the thing about seeing a 1986 classic on a proper movie screen: it's just better. Bigger. More fun in a crowd.

The Strand is showing Ferris Bueller's Day Off on Thursday August 20th, and if you have any nostalgia at all for Matthew Broderick staging the greatest fake sick day in cinema history, this is your Thursday night. The bonus is the live pre-show concert on the Strand's Mighty Allen Theatre Organ, which starts 30 minutes before the film. It's a whole experience, not just a movie. The Strand is already one of the best venues in Marietta for a night out, and this kind of event fits the room perfectly.

Life moves pretty fast. Get your tickets before this one sells out.
scoring_notes: Ferris Bueller came out in 1986, which means the East Cobb audience was roughly 12-18 years old at the time. This is peak nostalgia territory for a 42-year-old median-age crowd. The Strand's organ pre-show adds genuine uniqueness over a standard screening. Thursday night is a slight drag on urgency but the event date still falls within the publishing window. The Strand is a beloved local venue, which adds a neighborhood authenticity angle.

blurb:
Truist Park on a Saturday night in August is genuinely one of the better ways to spend an evening in Cobb County, and this weekend you've got a reason to go.

The Braves host the Arizona Diamondbacks on Saturday the 15th, first pitch at 7:15. It's a night game, so the heat backs off, the lights come on, and the Battery turns into exactly the kind of scene that makes you remember why you live five minutes from a Major League ballpark. Bring the family, bring some friends, or just go grab a seat and enjoy the game. There's no complicated calculus here.

Tickets are moving, so don't wait until Friday afternoon to figure it out.
scoring_notes: East Cobb is Braves country. Proximity to Truist Park is a genuine selling point for this audience, and a Saturday night home game is the most natural fit on the calendar. Families with teens love it, empty nesters love it, casual fans love it. Scores slightly lower on uniqueness since it's a regular-season game, not a playoff or rivalry matchup, but Saturday night format and the upcoming-Friday timing make it the most immediately actionable pick on the list.

blurb:
Batting practice from the outfield. New food. A former Braves player. Yeah, this is a good afternoon.

Bats & Bites at Truist Park on August 28th gets you early access to the ballpark, a guided behind-the-scenes tour that ends at the Outfield Market, a chance to meet and talk to a former Brave, and samples of new featured food plus a signature beer or cocktail. Then you head out to the outfield to watch batting practice, and if you're in the right spot at the right time, you might even catch a ball.

It runs 3pm to 7pm, which makes it a PERFECT way to kick off a Friday evening. This is the kind of experience that people who have been to a hundred Braves games haven't actually done. Don't sleep on it.
scoring_notes: Strong uniqueness score because this is a curated, behind-the-scenes experience with meet-and-greet access to a former player, not just a standard game ticket. East Cobb's Braves-country identity and $118K median income makes this a natural fit. The Friday afternoon timing and 3-7pm window works well for established adults and empty nesters who have flexibility in their schedules. Families with teens could enjoy this too. Slightly lower audience match than the Saturday night game because Friday afternoon access requires schedule flexibility.

venue: United Bankshares Amphitheater at Depot Park, Kennesaw
blurb:
Fleetwood Mac tribute acts get a bad reputation sometimes, but Rumours ATL is not your average cover band. They're the real deal, built specifically around recreating the sound and harmonies of one of rock's most beloved catalogs, and the reviews back it up.

The Kennesaw Concert Series brings them to the United Bankshares Amphitheater at Depot Park on Saturday August 22nd at 7pm, and admission is FREE. You're going to hear 'Rhiannon,' 'Go Your Own Way,' 'Dreams,' and more in an outdoor amphitheater setting on a summer evening. For an audience that grew up with Fleetwood Mac, this one hits different than a random local act.

Bring a chair or a blanket, get there a little early to stake out a good spot, and let the night take care of itself. There are very few better free events in Cobb County this month.
scoring_notes: Fleetwood Mac's peak era maps almost perfectly to East Cobb's median age of 42, and frankly it resonates even more for the empty-nester segment who are 50+. Free admission is a non-issue for this income bracket but makes it even easier to say yes. The outdoor amphitheater format is ideal for a warm August evening. Loses a uniqueness point because the Kennesaw Concert Series is a recurring series, but each performer is distinct and Rumours ATL is a specific, one-night-only date within it.

event_name: All Shook Up: The Elvis Presley Musical
venue: Marietta's Theatre in the Square, Marietta
blurb:
Shakespeare meets Elvis. And yeah, that's exactly as fun as it sounds.

All Shook Up is a jukebox musical comedy built around Elvis Presley's greatest hits, wrapped inside a retelling of Twelfth Night. It's 1955, a leather-jacketed stranger rolls into a sleepy Midwestern town, and nothing is the same after that. Theatre in the Square runs multiple performances this week, including Thursday through Saturday evenings and a Saturday matinee, so there are real options here for different schedules.

If you've got teenagers who think Elvis is ancient history, this is a fun way to prove them wrong. If you're going as a couple, it's a legitimately good night out. The show runs through the 22nd, but week one is always the energy. Don't wait on it.
scoring_notes: Elvis catalog has massive recognition for the 42-median-age crowd and the established family demographic. Multi-night run during the window gives flexibility. Theatre in the Square is a beloved local venue. Slightly lower uniqueness since the run extends beyond this week, but it's a strong cultural fit overall.
